article.title: Why Meetings Run Longer Than Planned

paragraphs.en: Many teams begin meetings with good intentions but finish later than expected. Participants may arrive with different ideas about the purpose, while the agenda contains more topics than the available time allows. A discussion that was supposed to produce one decision becomes a debate about several unrelated problems. The cost is not limited to the extra minutes on the calendar. People lose time for focused work, and those attending from different time zones may have their schedules disrupted. Understanding why meetings expand is the first step toward making them useful rather than simply shorter.
paragraphs.zh: 許多團隊開會時意圖良好，結束卻比預定時間晚。參與者對目的的理解不同，議程項目又超過時間所能容納。原本應作出一項決定的討論，變成多個無關問題的辯論。成本不只是行事曆多出的分鐘，還包括專注工作時間減少及跨時區成員行程受干擾。了解會議為何延長，是讓會議有用而非單純縮短的第一步。
paragraphs.ja: 会議は善意で始まっても予定より長引きやすい。目的の理解が異なり、議題が多すぎると、一つの意思決定が無関係な論点に広がる。延長は集中作業や時差のある参加者にも影響する。

paragraphs.en: One common problem is an unclear objective. A meeting to share information requires a different format from one designed to make a difficult choice. If participants do not know whether they are expected to listen, advise, or decide, they may spend time repeating background information. A useful invitation states the desired outcome and identifies which decisions are actually required. Documents can be circulated beforehand so that meeting time is reserved for questions and disagreements. This does not mean every participant must read a lengthy report. A concise summary with relevant evidence is often more practical.
paragraphs.zh: 常見問題是目標不清。資訊分享與艱難決策需要不同形式。如果與會者不知道自己要聽取、提供建議還是作決定，就可能重複背景資訊。有效邀請應說明期望成果與需要的決策。文件可提前傳閱，會議時間留給提問與分歧。這不代表人人都要閱讀冗長報告；附有相關證據的簡短摘要通常更實用。
paragraphs.ja: 目的が不明確だと説明が繰り返される。情報共有と意思決定では進め方が異なる。招集時に期待する成果を示し、資料を事前共有すると議論に時間を使える。

paragraphs.en: Another source of delay is the tendency to discuss every interesting question immediately. Someone raises a useful but secondary issue, and the group follows it without considering whether it belongs on the agenda. A facilitator can acknowledge the point, record it, and return to the original decision. This practice is sometimes called a parking lot for issues. It works only if the recorded questions are assigned an owner and a follow-up process; otherwise, participants may feel that their concerns have been ignored. Respectful redirection protects both the schedule and the quality of discussion.
paragraphs.zh: 另一延誤來源是每個有趣問題都立即討論。有人提出有用但次要的議題，團隊便偏離議程。主持人可承認其重要性、記錄並返回原決策。這有時稱為議題停車場。但記錄後須指定負責人和後續處理，否則成員可能覺得意見被忽視。尊重地引導回正題，既保護時間也維持討論品質。
paragraphs.ja: 興味深い話題にすぐ脱線することも多い。進行役は論点を記録して本題に戻す。後で扱う責任者と方法まで決めれば、参加者の意見を軽視せずに時間を守れる。

paragraphs.en: Decision-making rules also matter. A team may debate endlessly because nobody knows who has the authority to choose among alternatives. Consensus can be valuable, especially when implementation requires broad cooperation, but it is not always necessary for every operational detail. The meeting owner should explain which decisions require agreement and which will be made by a designated person after consultation. Clear criteria help participants evaluate options rather than defend personal preferences. When the evidence is insufficient, postponing a decision with a defined deadline may be more responsible than extending the meeting without direction.
paragraphs.zh: 決策規則也很重要。團隊可能因不知道誰有權選擇方案而無休止辯論。共識在需要廣泛合作時有價值，但不必每個操作細節都一致同意。會議負責人應說明哪些決策需取得共識，哪些由指定人員徵詢後決定。清楚標準能讓參與者評估方案而非捍衛偏好。證據不足時，訂定期限後延後決策，可能比無方向地延長會議更負責任。
paragraphs.ja: 決定権限が不明確だと議論が終わらない。全員の合意が必要な事項と、担当者が意見を聞いて決める事項を区別する。情報不足なら期限を定めて延期する方がよい場合もある。

paragraphs.en: Time estimates are often unrealistic. Complex decisions need more discussion than routine updates, yet agendas may allocate equal time to both. Organizers can review past meetings to understand which topics regularly overrun. A short buffer between sessions allows participants to take notes and move to their next commitment. Starting on time is useful, but ending on time requires active choices during the meeting. A facilitator may need to shorten an update, postpone a low-priority topic, or request a written response. These choices should be explained so they do not appear arbitrary.
paragraphs.zh: 時間估計往往不切實際。複雜決策比例行更新需要更多討論，議程卻可能平均分配。主辦者可回顧過往會議，找出經常超時的主題。場次之間留緩衝，讓成員記錄並前往下一個行程。準時開始有用，但準時結束需要會中主動取捨。主持人可能縮短更新、延後低優先議題或要求書面回覆，並說明原因以免顯得任意。
paragraphs.ja: 時間配分が非現実的なこともある。複雑な判断には多くの時間が必要だ。過去の会議を振り返り、余裕を設け、優先度の低い話題を延期する判断も必要になる。

paragraphs.en: The final minutes should be used to confirm what has been decided, who will act, and when progress will be reviewed. Without this step, a meeting may end on time but create additional confusion afterward. A short written record prevents participants from remembering different conclusions. It also reduces the need for another meeting to clarify basic responsibilities. Successful meetings are not measured only by duration. They are measured by whether the right people exchanged necessary information, made appropriate decisions, and left with a shared understanding of the next actions.
paragraphs.zh: 最後幾分鐘應確認決定事項、負責人與下次檢視時間。若省略這一步，即使準時結束，事後仍可能混亂。簡短書面紀錄可避免參與者記住不同結論，也能減少為釐清責任再開一次會的需要。成功會議不只看長短，而是看合適的人是否交換必要資訊、作出適當決策並理解下一步。
paragraphs.ja: 最後に決定事項、担当者、確認時期を整理する。記録がなければ後で認識がずれる。会議の成功は短さだけでなく、必要な情報交換と適切な決定、次の行動が明確かどうかで測る。
